title: Conjecture 5
statement_text: If $G$ is a planar graph of girth at least five on $n$ vertices, then $R_6(G)$ has diameter $O(n)$.
context_text: The reconfiguration graph $R_k(G)$ has as vertices all proper $k$-colourings of $G$, two colourings being adjacent if they differ in the colour of exactly one vertex (so paths in $R_k(G)$ correspond to recolouring vertices one at a time while keeping the colouring proper). Bousquet and Perarnau proved that for a $d$-degenerate graph on $n$ vertices and $c\ge2d+2$, $R_c(G)$ has diameter at most $(d+1)n$, while Bonamy et al. showed that $d+2$ colours may give quadratic diameter. A general lemma also shows that if a $d$-degenerate graph $G$ is colourable from every assignment of lists of size $c$, then for every independent set $I$, the diameter of $R_{c+d+1}(G)$ is at most $2(n+|I|)$ plus the diameter of $R_{c+d}(G-I)$. For planar graphs the authors obtain linear diameter with $10$ colours, and for triangle-free planar graphs with $7$ colours ($R_7(G)$ has diameter at most $7n$). Since planar graphs of girth at least five are colourable from lists of size three (Thomassen), the lemma together with the Bousquet–Perarnau theorem already gives linear diameter with $7$ colours, and the authors believe $6$ suffice; they suspect a variation of their method could prove it, but several complications arise. For girth at least six, the bound $6$ follows from 2-degeneracy and the Bousquet–Perarnau theorem.
paper_title: A Thomassen-type method for planar graph recoloring
